observed_title: A note on semi-infinite program bounding methods
version: Local arXiv:1912.01763v1 overlay December 4, 2019; internal title date December 5, 2019. Both observed dates retained.

read_ranges.scope: All five pages including references; no appendix. Original pp3–4 viewed for Lemma2, geometric counterexample and all proof inequalities; p2 also rendered.

topic_relevance.B02: direct: ordinary SIP lower-bound convergence with approximate separation and a counterexample to arbitrary positive violations.

definitions.name: Master and separation sign convention
definitions.statement: SIP minimizes f(x) over x∈X with g(x,y)≤0 for every y∈Y. g*(x)=sup_y g(x,y). The master keeps a finite nested Y_k and is globally minimized; master minima are lower bounds and nondecreasing.

theorem_cards.label: Counterexample to imported Lemma1: any positive violation does not suffice
assumptions: X=Y=[−1,1], f(x)=−x, g(x,y)=2x−y; empty initial index set.
At each iteration master is solved globally but chosen separating point is y_k=x_k rather than a fixed-quality worst violation.
theorem_cards.statement: True feasible set is [−1,−1/2] and optimum is 1/2. The selected sequence x_k=y_k=2^{1−k} has positive violation g=x_k, while lower bounds −2^{1−k} increase only to 0<1/2.
proof_steps: 作者反例：each selected y_k adds x≤y_k/2, giving the next exact master solution x_{k+1}=x_k/2.
本次核验：g*(x_k)=2x_k+1; the achieved ratio x_k/(2x_k+1) tends to zero. Thus the example has no single positive fractional accuracy valid for every iteration.
gaps: This refutes the claim quoted from source [4], not every approximate-oracle exchange method.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma2: fixed fractional separation gives qualitative lower-bound convergence
assumptions: Finite-dimensional compact nonempty host sets X,Y; real-valued continuous f and g on X and X×Y.
Initial Y_0 is finite, masters are solved globally, and Y_{k+1}=Y_k∪{y_k}.
One fixed α∈(0,1) works for all iterations: either certify g*(x_k)≤0 or return y_k∈Y with g(x_k,y_k)≥α g*(x_k)>0.
theorem_cards.statement: The restricted minima converge to the full SIP optimum. If a finite master is infeasible then the SIP is infeasible; if g*(x_k)≤0 then that master solution is already globally optimal. An infinite run has feasible optimal accumulation points and its entire monotone lower-bound sequence converges.
proof_steps: 作者证明：compactness and continuity give global master minimizers; later master points satisfy every older generated cut (pp3–4).
作者证明：take a convergent subsequence in X; uniform continuity of g on X×Y and old-cut feasibility imply selected violation g(x_k,y_k)→0 along that subsequence. The fixed α then gives g*(x_k)→0.
本次可自含补足：|sup_y g(x,y)−sup_y g(x′,y)|≤sup_y|g(x,y)−g(x′,y)|. Uniform continuity therefore proves continuity of g* without relying on the cited parametric-optimization theorem.

作者证明：the limit is feasible; f continuity and master lower-bound inequality make the limit objective equal f*. Monotonicity then transfers subsequence value convergence to the entire lower-bound sequence.
gaps: No iteration count, convergence rate, objective error bound from residual alone, or floating-point certificate is given.

Variable α_k→0, mere positivity, sampling and local lower-level solutions do not meet this theorem. Exact separation (α=1) fits the same proof, but α=1 is a local extension outside the printed α∈(0,1).
The infinite-run proof implicitly uses subsequence indices when writing k,ℓ; it does not assert convergence of all decision iterates to one point.

For an infeasible compact SIP, compactness gives some finite infeasible subfamily of all constraints, but does not show an adaptive oracle will generate it. Under the complete fixed-α/global-master Lemma2 hypotheses, an infinite nonempty-master run would instead produce a feasible accumulation point by the proof and is impossible. Thus finite infeasibility detection follows from the full lemma argument, with no iteration bound; it is not inferred from nested masters alone.

constant_dependence.explicit: One iteration-independent α>0 controls g*≤g/α. Continuity supplies an unspecified modulus on the compact product. No rate or finite tolerance iteration count is supplied.
constant_dependence.dependence: Any quantitative rate would need additional regularity, geometry and oracle/master accuracy assumptions not present here.

endpoint_limits: Noncompact host sets or discontinuous objective/constraint functions are outside the proof.
α_k tending to zero is not the fixed-α hypothesis.
Residual ε feasibility is separate from objective ε optimality.
reusable_methods: Keep master lower-bound monotonicity separate from convergence.
Demand an iteration-uniform quality guarantee on the violated constraint oracle.
Use compactness, old-cut persistence, uniform continuity and the support supremum inequality to close the qualitative proof.
unchecked: All local pages and references read; no external source [4] independently audited.
Section4 says the prior upper-bounding procedure still stands, but this is an author assertion about an external algorithm and is not promoted to an audited upper-bound theorem.
No algorithmic complexity, numerical solver behavior or center-cube transfer asserted.

local_repairs.repair: Uniform continuity plus |sup a−sup b|≤sup|a−b| proves continuity of g*. The mathematical conclusion is preserved.
